newsitem.title: FRANCE: Murdoch could join up with France's TPS.
newsitem.headline: Murdoch could join up with France's TPS.

text.p: It is possible that Australian-born media mogul Rupert Murdoch could enter the share capital of the Television Par Satellite (TPS) French digital satellite television venture, the TPS head said on Thursday.
"Yes, there are various foreign players. The share capital of TPS could be opened to one of them; why not Rupert Murdoch," Patrick Le Lay told journalists during a news conference.
Le Lay is chairman of commercial broadcaster TF1 which has a 25 percent stake in TPS.
He also chairs the venture with state-owned France Television, Lyonnaise des Eaux, M6, Luxembourg's CLT and France Telecom.

TPS is scheduled to launch its digital service at December 16. In France, Canal Plus unit Canalsatellite is the main rival in digital television, up and running since March this year and privately held AB Productions is also broadcasting digital television programmes via satellite.
Murdoch's News Corp and the BSkyB satellite television group were earlier this year allied to Canal Plus and Bertelsmann for digital television in Germany.
But this deal fell through after the merger announcement between Bertelsmann's UFA and Luxembourg's CLT. Bertelsmann has dropped its German digital satellite plans, leaving the field to Leo Kirch.
Canal Plus has since announced a plan to merge with Nethold, a Dutch-based group controlled by the Swiss-South African Richemont group.

TPS is busy buying up film rights to feed the programmes of its many future channels, as well as taking out sports rights. But Le Lay recently lost a legal attempt to block a new multi-year deal between Canal Plus and the French soccer assocation, giving pay-per-view rights to Canalsatellite.
TF1 and Canal Plus are both shareholders of the Eurosports specialised satellite broadcaster.
BSkyB has obtained major British sports broadcasting rights.
